claims.says: the example boots and deploys locally
tf-check fails an unformatted root and names the file
only the roots a change touches are planned
one note groups many plans
the report is JSON and HTML, and links every root to its full plan
destroys and outliers are open, identical groups are folded
each wave goes out only once approved
a wave whose plans changed after approval applies nothing
a wave counts only an approval sealed by a key the signers file lists
drift is reported by root
a module version rolls out one pull request per wave
changed modules are published at a new version
tips are on by default and name their rule
with no more than a drift schedule and the canary wave in terragucci.yml, init writes the same pipeline
two pushes to main apply one after the other, and the commit carries one terragucci/apply status
a control repo opens one pull request per project that changes, and the merged pipeline applies
each plan run is one trace, with a span per root and the binary spans inside it
the metrics of a plan run reach Prometheus with the counts in its report
init finds Terragrunt and its 15 units on its own and writes the pipeline the Terragrunt example commits
the Terragrunt example boots, applying the canary wave before the rest with one run --all each
tf-check fails an unformatted Terragrunt file and names it
only the units a change reaches are planned, including a file a module reads that Terragrunt misses
a dependency whose mock_outputs can stand in for apply is named by a tip
a unit whose plan would read mock_outputs is not planned; it waits for its upstream to apply
a new upstream and its dependent merge together and apply in order, so no mock reaches real state
drift is reported by unit in a Terragrunt repo, with the same tracking issue
a refused wave names each root whose plan moved and the attributes that moved
a failed apply is triaged from the known-error table
drift on a literal becomes a pull request with the live value, and import blocks for what is unmanaged
each tip becomes its own small pull request
fmt on request commits to the pull request branch and nowhere else
release notes come from the conventional commits that touched the module
on a fresh estate the plan job holds back a root whose upstream is unapplied, names it in the report, and stays green
a Forgejo job gets an OIDC token Forgejo signed for its repo and ref, and trades it for the plan or apply role
tf-apply runs as a turn on a fountain steward, started by the forge job, and applies every root
an opt-in policy denies a plan, fails the root in tf-plan, and names the violation
a pull request comment re-plans on request and never applies, and a root outside the configured ones is refused
a plan that waits for a state lock another plan holds shows the wait as a State lock wait span, in its report and its trace
the Pipeline health dashboard init writes shows the runs, errors and results of a plan, a drift run and a gated wave
the Change review dashboard init writes shows the roots, groups and changes by action of a pull request
the Rollouts and waves dashboard init writes shows a wave waiting for its approval, how long, and wave runs by result
the Drift dashboard init writes shows the roots a drift run found drifted and how old the drift is
the Estate dashboard init writes shows the roots of a project and the binary and terragucci versions it runs
the Runs dashboard init writes shows the slowest roots, stage durations and the trace of each run from Tempo
the SLO dashboards init writes are provisioned, and the plan SLO records the plans of a project from the rules init writes

the plan note links the report in the bucket, the report links each root plan and the trace of the run, the trace and the dashboards link back to the report, and the index row links the commit, pull request and job
a tf-apply wave whose plan the policy denies applies nothing, and its report keeps the changes of the denied root with the denial and the warnings
tf-check fails with the cause in its log for a validate error, a failing policy test and a choudoufu live-check refusal
a re-plan comment for a root the pull request does not reach is answered that it is not affected and plans nothing, and a re-plan whose forge call fails fails its job with the cause
with respond.drift: attribute, tf-drift lists who changed each drifted attribute under its root in the drift issue
with respond.version-bump: suggest, the version-bump job of the pipeline runs after the last apply on the default branch and opens a release pull request with the answer of the decision service
the plan of each Terragrunt unit sends its spans to the report through the TG_TF_PATH wrapper, and waits up to five minutes for the state lock
a job with oidc.gcp and oidc.azure gets an external_account file and the ARM_* variables the google and azurerm providers read, with a token for the audience of each cloud
a comment on a merged pull request re-runs its apply from the merge commit, applies a wave only once its approval is sealed, and refuses an open pull request and a commenter with no write access

a /terragucci agent comment pushes the commit of the stand-in agent to the branch of the pull request, which re-plans it and is linked in the reply, and a forbidden path, a non-writer and a fork push nothing
